column1: # THE TEMPLATE SURFACE -- a generator written in the target's own
# `src` is the template file. `out` is its canonical aontu form, and
# `back` is the template the round trip answers: `src` itself wherever
# the sugar is already the fixpoint of the two transforms (D6), and the
# normalised spelling where it is not. Both directions ride one row,
# because a transform pinned in one direction only is half a transform.
# ONE RULE (D1): a marked line is aontu source, and every other line is
# a line of output -- one quoted string, landing wherever the marker
# lines left a list open. Nothing here parses aontu, and nothing reads
# the target's syntax beyond its comment token.
# THE MARKER IS THE TARGET'S COMMENT TOKEN PLUS A DASH (D2), recognised
# after leading whitespace and keeping its own indentation, which is
# what lets a template be written where its output appears (D7).
# `ask.marker` names it; absent, it is the C-family `//-`.
# THE CANONICAL QUOTE IS CHOSEN PER LINE (D6): a backtick unless the
# line holds one, and then the double quote with `"` escaped. A
# BACKSLASH IS ESCAPED IN EITHER, because this engine reads the escapes
# of a backtick string exactly as it reads a quoted one.
# WHITESPACE IS THE ARTIFACT OF RECORD (D8): a blank line, a line of
# two spaces and a line of one tab are output, and the canonical form
# quotes each explicitly so an editor that trims on save is caught.
# THE SUGAR IS THE FIXPOINT OF THE TWO TRANSFORMS (D6): a canonical line
# is rebuilt as a target line only when desugaring the rebuild answers
# the canonical line back, so a line no target line can carry -- one
# that would itself read as a marker -- stays where it is, and there is
# no table of escapes to get wrong.

column1: # THE BLOCK FORM IS NOT ONLY C'S. A marker's closer is implied for the

# holds no space, so a marker may carry its own closer after one. That
